groups.title: [AppSec #527] Seal controller execution and launch policy
groups.label: enhancement
groups.body:
Parent: #527

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-01:** Do not grant execution authority to target-supplied `.smithers` code.
- **R-03:** Enforce operator-owned credential-name and provider-home policy.
- **R-07:** Scope provider credentials per child in multi-provider local runs.
- **R-08:** Enforce `prompt_review_required` at launch, bound to an effective-configuration digest.
- **R-25:** Replace wildcard `SMITHERS_*` forwarding with a named allowlist.

## Security outcome

Authenticate the controller execution closure, keep executable runner state operator-owned, bind launch acknowledgement to the exact inputs being executed, constrain provider-home paths, and ensure each child receives only the controller and provider environment it needs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pre-existing target-owned executable `.smithers` content cannot become the controller execution source.
- Generated runner/adapters are sealed or verified before import; unsupported custom adapters fail closed unless explicitly acknowledged against their digest.
- Repository configuration cannot silently select arbitrary host credential names or provider-home paths.
- Launch fails when the required prompt/config/topology/reference/commit acknowledgement is missing or stale.
- Multi-provider child environments omit inactive provider credentials and forward only documented controller variables.
- Regression tests cover hostile pre-existing runner files, stale acknowledgements, credential-name/path policy, and environment isolation.

## Non-goal

Do **not** disable or constrain agent YOLO/bypass-permissions execution. No sandbox, command allowlist, network allowlist, or in-run approval prompt is introduced. D-01 through D-04 remain accepted residual risks.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.

groups.title: [AppSec #527] Add campaign data governance and durable approvals
groups.label: enhancement
groups.body:
Parent: #527

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-04:** Add campaign sensitivity classification and provider/cloud disclosure acknowledgement.
- **R-09:** Require durable human signoff bound to the final-report and materialization digests.
- **R-26:** Require a separate operator acknowledgement for private eval artifact upload.

## Security outcome

Make data destinations, private-source handling, human acceptance, and private artifact publication explicit operator decisions with immutable provenance rather than repository-controlled assertions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Campaigns default to private sensitivity and record allowed source/artifact destinations plus the governing policy digest.
- Provider/cloud disclosure acknowledgement is operator-owned, names the destination, and becomes stale when its bound policy/input digest changes.
- Publication-sensitive materialization requires durable reviewer signoff bound to target, graph, report, and selected artifact digests.
- Private eval payload upload requires a distinct operator acknowledgement naming target, destination, included files, and retention policy.
- Reports distinguish structural verification, model consensus, executable reproduction, and human acceptance.
- Documentation states the data-handling basis and relevant residual risks without claiming controls that cannot be enforced.

## Non-goal

Agent YOLO/bypass-permissions execution remains unchanged. This group adds pre-launch and output/publication governance, not in-run approval gates or execution containment.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.

groups.title: [AppSec #527] Make artifacts and local credentials secret-safe
groups.label: bug
groups.body:
Parent: #527

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-02:** Add a universal fail-closed secret gate before canonical artifact publication.
- **R-05:** Expand secret patterns, add a high-entropy fallback, and thread exact run secrets through at-rest checks.
- **R-18:** Stop writing the Kimi API key to persistent cleartext configuration.
- **R-28:** Ignore common local secret/key file names.

## Security outcome

Prevent known or pattern-detected secrets from entering publishable artifacts, improve defense-in-depth for at-rest evidence, and remove avoidable cleartext credential persistence.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every agent-controlled canonical output and companion artifact is scanned before publication using maintained patterns and exact known secret values.
- Contaminated artifacts fail closed; if raw evidence must remain immutable, any redacted derivative is explicit and manifest-linked rather than silently rewriting canonical bytes.
- Redaction covers the approved key/token/mnemonic/URL/entropy cases with state, event, and attempt-ledger tests.
- Kimi API-key auth avoids persistent cleartext configuration and cleans unavoidable transient state on normal and signal exits.
- `.gitignore` covers `.env*`, `.envrc`, common PEM/key/container formats, and `id_rsa`.
- Documentation describes redaction as best-effort defense in depth, not a completeness guarantee.

## Non-goal

No mediated agent filesystem, sandbox, or network restriction is introduced; agent YOLO behavior remains unchanged.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.

groups.title: [AppSec #527] Harden dashboard authentication, privacy, errors, and CSP
groups.label: bug
groups.body:
Parent: #527

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-06:** Stop returning the dashboard session token from an unauthenticated route; authenticate reads and SSE too.
- **R-19:** Redact raw stdout, stderr, and rendered-prompt data on the dashboard path.
- **R-27:** Fail closed when an API request omits `Host`.
- **R-31:** Return generic unexpected errors with correlation IDs and retain redacted server-side detail.
- **R-32:** Require explicit confirmation before dashboard run launch.
- **R-36:** Remove unused `data:` image allowance from CSP.
- **R-37:** Add CSP violation visibility in development and CI.

## Security outcome

Make the loopback dashboard capability-based for every API surface, minimize sensitive evidence disclosure, harden request validation and error handling, and lock down/test its browser policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- The session token is delivered out of band and never appears in `/api/session`; reads, mutations, and SSE require it.
- Missing or non-loopback `Host`, invalid Origin, and cross-site requests fail closed.
- Dashboard evidence fields are redacted before response, with at-rest redaction used where compatible with immutable artifact contracts.
- Unexpected failures return a generic message plus correlation ID; server diagnostics are redacted.
- Run launch requires an audited confirmation that shows target, providers, and configured budget.
- CSP uses `img-src 'self'` unless a tested dependency proves otherwise, and integration coverage observes unexpected policy violations.
- Regression tests exercise token disclosure, authenticated reads/SSE, request context, redaction, confirmation, errors, and CSP.

## Non-goal

This does not change agent YOLO/bypass-permissions execution. Dashboard launch confirmation occurs before dispatch and is not an in-run agent approval.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.

groups.title: [AppSec #527] Enforce dependency and Git supply-chain policy
groups.label: enhancement
groups.body:
Parent: #527

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-10:** Upgrade/replace vulnerable `adm-zip` and add malicious-archive regression coverage.
- **R-11:** Add a production dependency advisory gate with recorded, expiring exceptions.
- **R-20:** Lock down Git transports and reject option-like or unsafe repository/ref inputs.
- **R-34:** Adopt and enforce one direct-dependency pinning policy.
- **R-35:** Periodically record and review publisher/provenance drift for critical tools.
- **R-38:** Make EVMBench Dockerfile interpolation structurally safe.

## Security outcome

Make dependency resolution, advisory disposition, source transport, generated build commands, and publisher identity auditable and resistant to mutable or option-injected inputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- No production resolution uses vulnerable `adm-zip` 0.5.18; archive limits and malformed ZIP regressions remain enforced.
- CI/release validation blocks actionable reachable High/Critical production advisories unless an explicit unexpired exception is recorded.
- Git calls explicitly disable unsafe transports, use operand separators where supported, and reject `ext::`, `file::`, and leading-option inputs.
- Workspace direct dependencies follow one documented pinning policy checked in CI.
- A periodic non-blocking job records publisher/maintainer/provenance changes for the named critical packages and escalates drift.
- EVMBench Dockerfile generation structurally separates or centrally validates/quotes all shell-interpolated values.
- Regression tests cover archive abuse, dependency policy, Git transport/argument cases, and Dockerfile interpolation.

## Non-goal

No agent command or network allowlist is added; agent YOLO/bypass-permissions behavior remains unchanged.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.

groups.title: [AppSec #527] Harden Modal image, credential, bundle, and shell boundaries
groups.label: enhancement
groups.body:
Parent: #527

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-12:** Integrity-pin the Modal base image, toolchain downloads, and global installs; record a material manifest/SBOM.
- **R-13:** Exchange Kimi refresh credentials for short-TTL access tokens and scope credential volumes per row.
- **R-17:** Reject redirects on Kimi OAuth refresh.
- **R-24:** Add a self-contained traversal guard to the staged public-bundle writer.
- **R-29:** Remove or quote shell interpolation in the Modal smoke harness.

## Security outcome

Make the cloud execution image reproducible, reduce credential lifetime and cross-row exposure, and harden Modal bundle and command construction without changing the agent execution model.

## Acceptance criteria

- Base images and downloaded toolchains are immutable/integrity-verified; unlocked global installs and unchecked downloads fail CI.
- Image provenance includes a machine-readable material manifest or SBOM and immutable fingerprint.
- Kimi subscription handling sends only a controller-obtained short-TTL access token where supported, uses per-row credential volume isolation, and rejects refresh redirects.
- Public-bundle writes locally reject absolute and traversal paths before filesystem mutation.
- Smoke commands pass provider/phase structurally or quote them with the shared helper.
- Regression tests cover integrity policy, credential row separation, OAuth redirects, traversal, and shell metacharacters.

## Non-goal

Modal agents continue to run in the required YOLO/bypass-permissions mode. No sandbox, egress allowlist, command allowlist, or in-run approval prompt is added.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.

groups.title: [AppSec #527] Enforce resource ceilings and bounded pricing fetches
groups.label: bug
groups.body:
Parent: #527
Related operational resource issue: #607

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-14:** Add enforced per-run token/spend and request/turn/context ceilings that abort.
- **R-15:** Enforce an absolute eval-matrix row cap before resolution or materialization.
- **R-16:** Bound, validate, stream-limit, and reject redirects for pricing-catalog fetches.

## Security outcome

Turn reported resource usage into enforceable limits, bound combinatorial eval work before allocation, and prevent the configurable pricing fetch from becoming an unbounded or unsafe network read.

## Acceptance criteria

- Configuration supports enforced run cost/token budgets; exhaustion aborts deterministically and is durable evidence.
- Per-attempt/run request, turn, output, and context byte ceilings are enforced at the relevant boundaries.
- Eval target × variant × trial products are overflow-safe and rejected above a documented absolute cap before target resolution, allocation, iteration, or writes; JSON Schema and runtime schema remain in parity.
- Pricing URLs require safe HTTPS origins, reject credentials/query/fragment and local/private/metadata destinations, and use `redirect: 'error'`.
- Pricing bodies are counted incrementally and cancelled one byte over the cap, including chunked and dishonest-length responses.
- Boundary tests cover exact/over limits, cancellation, redirects, timeouts, multiplicative overflow, and budget exhaustion.

## Non-goal

These are controller-side admission and accounting limits. Agent YOLO/bypass-permissions behavior and unrestricted in-run commands/network remain unchanged. This issue is related to but does not claim to resolve the scratch-directory lifecycle in #607.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.

groups.title: [AppSec #527] Harden references, paths, and materialization boundaries
groups.label: bug
groups.body:
Parent: #527

Audit snapshot: `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380`
Implementation base: `d5981c83620e365d1427e2d647c682a93aec3a52`

## Approved recommendations

- **R-21:** Fence and label Markdown reference bodies as untrusted data.
- **R-22:** Case-normalize protected-root and sensitive-path matching.
- **R-23:** Close the materialization overwrite symlink-swap race.
- **R-30:** Rename or unify colliding `validateSafeId` APIs so result contracts cannot be confused/discarded.
- **R-33:** Make prompt-frontmatter plain-object checks prototype-safe.

## Security outcome

Clarify untrusted reference boundaries and make path, overwrite, identifier-validation, and object-shape checks deterministic across case-insensitive filesystems and hostile inputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Markdown references are explicitly labeled/fenced as untrusted content before prompt handoff.
- Protected-root and sensitive-segment checks normalize Unicode and case consistently, with mixed-case regressions.
- Overwrite materialization cannot follow a destination swapped to a symlink between validation and write.
- Safe-ID APIs have unambiguous names/contracts and call sites cannot silently discard policy results.
- Frontmatter accepts only objects with `Object.prototype` or `null` prototypes.
- Tests cover prompt injection delimiters, Unicode/case variants, symlink races, safe-ID misuse, and custom prototypes.

## Non-goal

No mediated filesystem layer or agent sandbox is introduced; agent YOLO/bypass-permissions access remains unchanged.

Post-remediation ARI will be measured only on the combined candidate; this issue does not claim a standalone score change.
